conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, Compliance Division. My name is Agent Parker. I'm calling regarding an urgent issue related to your federal income taxes. With whom am I speaking?
Uh, this is Jamie. Is this really the IRS? I, um, got a message telling me to call about my taxes.

Yes, Jamie, this is the IRS. Our records show serious discrepancies in your tax filings for the last three years, resulting in unpaid balances and substantial penalties. Did you receive any previous notices?
I-I'm not sure. I just graduated last year and I'm still figuring out how taxes work. I haven't really gotten any letters, I think.
That's understandable, but unfortunately, the system has flagged you for nonpayment. If this isn't handled immediately, it will escalate into a federal matter. Do you understand the severity of this?
Oh my god, I didn't realize. I can't get in trouble, I have student loans and barely any money. Am I going to get fined or something?

Jamie, the consequences include heavy fines, the freezing of your bank accounts, liens on your assets, wage garnishments, and even criminal referral. These actions begin automatically if this isn't resolved today.
Wait, what? You can freeze my bank account? I can't lose my account, I need it for my rent and everything.

Unless you settle your tax debt right now, enforcement will begin. I want to help you avoid further penalties, but you must cooperate fully and not hang up this call or speak to anyone else during this process.
Okay, I'll do whatever you say, just please don't freeze my account. How much do I owe?
According to the file, your total balance is $3,721.48, including back taxes, compounded interest, and processing fees. Immediate payment is required to prevent further escalation.
I don't have that much. I'm already struggling with my loan payments. I don't know what to do.

Let me be clear: if you do not act right now, a bench warrant will be issued for your arrest, and your credit will be destroyed. Do you have access to any funds, such as savings, credit cards, or mobile payment apps?
I have a little savings and a credit card, but my limit isn't high. Can I pay in installments or something?

The IRS cannot accept installments at this stage. However, we can process an immediate settlement if you send the available amount today using a verified method. This is your only chance to avoid legal action.
Okay, what do I need to do? I can maybe pay about $1,000 today.

That will temporarily halt enforcement actions. Here's what you must do: you will need to purchase $1,000 in Target or Apple gift cards from a nearby store and stay on the line with me while you do so. Do not discuss this with anyone, the matter is confidential under federal law.
Gift cards? I thought you'd want a check or something.

For urgent compliance, we process payments via government-approved settlement cards. Do not question the process. Get the cards, scratch off the back, and read me the codes. This is the only way to resolve your tax debt today.
Okay, I'll go to the store right now. Please promise you won't send the police or anything.
As long as you follow my instructions exactly, your account will be flagged as compliant, and you will not face arrest or legal proceedings. Are you leaving for the store now?
Yes, I'm going now. Should I call you back or stay on the line?
Stay on the line at all times. If you disconnect, the system might trigger enforcement actions automatically. Notify me when you arrive at the store.
Okay, I'm leaving now. Please just don't do anything to my account, I'm really scared.
Remain calm and cooperate. As soon as I receive the codes, your file will be updated and enforcement will be stopped.
